transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Time: 4:00pm PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO - BrightHealth), Oscar (Eng Lead), Priya (ML Eng), Samir (Security)

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: All right everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Sofia, I'm the AE for this account, Evan and Daniel are our SEs. Today we'll do a live walk through of chat & generative params, show streaming behavior and the Console Optimize suggestions. we'll leave time for Q&A. Maya, want to kick us off with goals?

[00:18] Maya Patel: Yeah thanks Sofia. main thing for BrightHealth is we want low latency triage responses in our clinician chat assistant. target is sub 300ms median for short responses, and cost per interactive session needs to stay under a threshold. also big ask: we process PHI in some flows so controls and auditability matter.

[00:37] Evan Cho: Great context. two quick clarifiers — is PHI going to be sent to hosted APIs or do you expect to keep it in a VPC/private deployment?

[00:44] Oscar Rivera: Initially hosted for speed, but if the PII/PHI ratio grows we need a private option or dedicated capacity. we want to understand the tradeoffs — latency, cost, and what changes in the API.

[00:56] Daniel Park: totally. so we'll demo hosted API behavior and console suggestions, and then call out how Dedicated/Private would differ — e.g., predictable throughput, VPC peering, customer KMS integration.

[01:12] Sofia Martinez: quick housekeeping: transcript may have small errors — sometimes 'KV cache' becomes 'K V cat' in these exports.

[01:20] Evan Cho: ok jumping in — live demo screen share — I'll start with a simple chat generation. calling the Generations/Chat endpoint with stream:true, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9, max_tokens 64. watch the partial events come back.

[01:38] [Sound of typing / screen share]

[01:44] Evan Cho: (demo) sending a clinician prompt "Summarize this patient's recent labs and highlight urgent items". first chunk arrives at ~150ms, then incremental deltas until the final chunk. note how tokens are flushed in small deltas — this helps UI progressive display.

[02:05] Priya Singh: Is the 150ms stable? our internal tests show variance at different times.

[02:12] Evan Cho: depends on model choice, sequence length, and batching. for short replies with 64 max_tokens you'll see sub-300ms median on hosted in the nearest region most times — but peak QPS and batching can add latency. we can pin models or use Dedicated for tighter SLOs. also mention that continuous batching helps throughput but can add a tiny tail latency.

[02:42] Oscar Rivera: what's the default fallback behavior if a stream connection drops mid-answer?

[02:48] Daniel Park: good question. we recommend client-side reconnect with an idempotency_key per request. when you reconnect, Redwood will attempt to continue if the server has the in-flight state, otherwise it will return the last committed token and you can resume or request a fresh generation. we also show sequence numbers in the stream events so UX can dedupe duplicates.

[03:14] Samir Khan: so are those logs accessible for audit? we need to map events back to request IDs for compliance.

[03:22] Evan Cho: yes — request IDs surface in the header and the Console has request-level traces. Dedicated/Private adds long-term audit retention and forwarding to your SIEM; for hosted we provide exportable logs and a redactable transcript layer.

[03:40] Maya Patel: you mentioned retry/backoff. can you show examples of exponential backoff and explain idempotency?

[03:47] Evan Cho: sure. quick code snippet: client sends idempotency_key UUID; on network error retry with exponential backoff (e.g., 200ms, 600ms, 1800ms) and cap retries — don't retry non-idempotent operations like streaming with partial state unless you can resume. for button-triggered single-shot generations, idempotency prevents double charges/duplicate outputs. Daniel will paste a sample runbook after the call.

[04:15] [Background noise / rustle] 

[04:21] Daniel Park: pasting runbook now in chat: "Use idempotency_key, check request status endpoint, use reconnect header X-Resume-From and server-provided resume token" — note this is paraphrased, actual header names may differ.

[04:40] Priya Singh: how do we handle partial transcript consistency when we have multiple retries? sometimes the UI shows overlapping tokens.

[04:48] Evan Cho: sequence numbers + client-side state machine: treat each stream chunk as append-only using sequence indices; on reconnect compare the last seq you saw with the server's last seq. if mismatch, request replay of tokens or discard duplicates. we provide example libraries that abstract this.

[05:10] Oscar Rivera: model params — you demoed temperature 0.2 earlier. for clinical notes where accuracy matters, what's recommended?

[05:17] Evan Cho: for deterministic outputs lower temperature (0.0–0.3) and narrower top_p (0.8–0.95). also use presence/penalty and system-level guardrails. we recommend adding eval prompt sets to the Console Optimize module so you can monitor quality regressions when you change a model or quantization profile.

[05:45] Sofia Martinez: quick Console tour — Daniel can show the Optimize tab with recent suggestions.

[05:52] Daniel Park: (screen share) here's Optimize: it shows token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency percentiles, and suggested quantization profiles based on your workload. for example, it flagged that for short chat turns a lower-precision int8 variant gave similar quality and 30% cost savings. you can accept suggestions or run a Canary with a percent rollout.

[06:18] Maya Patel: can Optimize automatically change batching for us or is it advisory?

[06:23] Daniel Park: advisory — it suggests changes and gives estimated cost/latency impact. we leave the decision to the customer —you can enable auto-apply in Dedicated if you want programmatic tuning, but customers generally prefer manual canary first.

[06:36] Priya Singh: about quantization — does the hosted model library expose int8 vs fp16 variants? we sometimes see hallucination regressions with aggressive quant.

[06:46] Evan Cho: yes, model catalog indicates precision. Optimize includes quality delta metrics on your eval set; if quality drops beyond threshold, you get an alert and automatic rollback options. also you'll see suggested prompts to mitigate hallucination like chain-of-thought constraints or anchor facts.

[07:12] Oscar Rivera: security — Samir has a long list of Qs but top-level: how is customer data encrypted and is there KMS integration?

[07:21] Samir Khan: and can we bring our own keys with Dedicated?

[07:25] Evan Cho: Hosted supports server-side encryption; you can redact and set retention windows. Dedicated and Private support BYOK with KMS/HSM, and Private offers full control for air-gapped deployments. we'll send SOC 2 and KMS integration docs after this call.

[07:42] Samir Khan: do you have automated artifact retention for transcripts? we need 3 years for audit trails — but we also may need auto-purge for PII flows.

[07:51] Daniel Park: yes both directions — customizable retention policies per workspace and per-route. for PII you can enable no-log endpoints that avoid persisting transcripts.

[08:06] Maya Patel: back on retries — what's Redwood's recommended pattern for client SDKs?

[08:11] Evan Cho: use short idempotent retries for HTTP 5xx and timeouts, backoff cap, and for streaming implement resume tokens. we also advise on a token-cost-aware retry budget to avoid runaway costs during flapping network conditions.

[08:32] Oscar Rivera: can you demo a reconnect?

[08:35] Evan Cho: yep — I'll forcibly drop the network from my client stub, then reattach. you'll see the server respond with last_seq: 18 and a resume token. the client calls resume endpoint with key and server streams the remaining tokens.

[08:56] [short pause, simulated disconnect noise] 

[09:04] Evan Cho: reconnect completed, final chunk arrived. note the UX delta was minimal.

[09:12] Priya Singh: nice — in our infra we can't accept duplicate messages. are there headers for dedupe?

[09:18] Daniel Park: yes we include request_id and idempotency_key headers; we also surface a "stream-seq" numbering. your server can drop anything with seq <= last_processed_seq.

[09:35] Maya Patel: ops questions: what's the SLA for hosted vs dedicated?

[09:40] Sofia Martinez: hosted has best-effort SLAs in trial; Dedicated includes an SLA with uptime and latency targets defined in the contract. we'll attach the SLA PDF in follow-up.

[09:50] Samir Khan: do you integrate with our SIEM? we need audit log forwarding and SSO/SAML for RBAC.

[09:58] Evan Cho: yes — SSO/SAML is supported, RBAC with route-level permissions, and logs can be forwarded via syslog or secure streaming to your SIEM. Dedicated/Private gives more control over log retention.

[10:12] Oscar Rivera: any advice on cost control for chat-heavy products?

[10:18] Daniel Park: leverage KV/prefix caching for common context, shorter max_tokens for short-turn UIs, use Optimize suggestions for quantization and batching, and set per-route quota and token budgets in Console. also we recommend sampling logs for quality metrics rather than storing full transcripts by default.

[10:36] Priya Singh: can we set per-route fallback policies in case the top model is busy? like degrade to a smaller variant?

[10:42] Evan Cho: absolutely — routing policies let you specify fallbacks by model family or by cost tier. if a region is saturated we can fallback to a lower-cost variant or route to another region per your policy.

[10:56] Maya Patel: demo wrap up — any gotchas for first 2-week POC?

[11:02] Sofia Martinez: yes: 1) start with a narrow eval prompt set, 2) pin a single model variant for the POC, 3) use client idempotency and a small retry budget, 4) instrument latency and token cost in Console. we'll provide a checklist.

[11:18] Oscar Rivera: timeline — we want to run a 2-week POC and then decide about Dedicated by end of Q2.

[11:25] Sofia Martinez: noted. we'll send a proposed POC plan and kickoff times.

[11:32] Priya Singh: small nit — any rate limiting patterns to avoid 429 storms?

[11:37] Daniel Park: enforce per-client quotas, implement token-leaky-bucket client-side, and on server 429s use jittered backoff. Console also shows request heatmaps so you can spot hotspots.

[11:55] Maya Patel: thanks this was helpful. can you also share a sample contract with Dedicated pricing ranges so we can budget?

[12:02] Sofia Martinez: yes — I'll include a price band and a sample MSA; these are placeholders but will help with internal approvals.

[12:10] [closing remarks, small talk] 

[12:25] Sofia Martinez: quick recap of next steps — I'll send pricing and security docs; Evan/Daniel will share runbook and replay code samples; Priya will drop prompt set and targets; we'll schedule a 30-min POC kickoff week of 3/8.

[12:40] Maya Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone.

[12:46] End of meeting.
